purpose: Irinotecan is a chemotherapy medicine used mainly to treat colorectal cancer (cancer of the colon or rectum). It is also used for some other cancers, such as pancreatic cancer. It is often given when other treatments have not worked or as part of a combination with other chemotherapy drugs.
how_it_works: Cancer cells grow by making copies of themselves, which requires their DNA to be untangled and copied. Irinotecan blocks a special protein called topoisomerase I that cancer cells need to untangle their DNA. When this protein is blocked, the DNA breaks and the cancer cells cannot copy themselves, so they die. Healthy cells can also be affected, which is why side effects occur.
common_side_effects: Diarrhea (can be severe — very important to treat quickly), nausea and vomiting, stomach cramps, hair loss, feeling very tired or weak, loss of appetite, low blood cell counts (which can raise infection risk and cause anemia), mouth sores, and sweating or flushing during the infusion.
warnings: Diarrhea is the most dangerous side effect — there are two types: one that happens during or right after the infusion (treat with atropine) and one that starts days later (treat immediately with loperamide and call your doctor). Low white blood cell counts increase your risk of serious infections, so tell your doctor right away if you have a fever. This drug should not be used during pregnancy as it can harm the baby. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, as many drugs can interact with irinotecan. People with a certain genetic variation (UGT1A1*28) may break down this drug more slowly and have worse side effects.
typical_dosing: Irinotecan is given as an IV infusion (drip into a vein) in a clinic or hospital, usually over 30 to 90 minutes. The dose and schedule depend on your cancer type and treatment plan — common schedules are once every 3 weeks, once a week for several weeks, or every 2 weeks as part of a combination regimen. Your doctor will determine the right dose based on your body size, kidney and liver function, and overall health.
